questions.stem: The variant c.621C>A changes codon UAC (Tyr) to UAA. What type of variant is this?
questions.explanation: UAA is a stop codon, so translation ends early (p.Tyr207X). The slide writes this as c.621U>A; in c. notation DNA bases are used and the changed base is C. A: Synonymous keeps the same amino acid. B: Frameshift needs an indel not divisible by 3. C: Missense substitutes a different amino acid. E: The change is within a codon, not a splice site.

questions.stem: A report reads c.16_17delAG (p.Ser6ProfsX2). Which best describes this variant?

options.A: Frameshift deletion with a premature stop

questions.explanation: Deleting 2 nt shifts the reading frame; 'fs' means frameshift and 'X2' means the stop is at position 2 of the shifted frame (Pro6 = 1, stop at codon 7). B: In-frame deletions remove a multiple of 3 nt. C: Nonsense is a single-base substitution creating a stop. D: Pro6 is only the first changed residue; the frame stays shifted after it. E: The protein is altered.

questions.stem: In the variant c.133C>T (p.Arg45Trp), what do the prefixes c. and p. indicate?

options.B: c. = coding DNA numbering; p. = protein level
options.C: c. = codon number; p. = polypeptide length

questions.explanation: c. numbers the coding DNA (cDNA) sequence and p. gives the protein change. A: Here p. is the protein level, not the short chromosome arm. C: 133 is a nucleotide position; the codon number (45) is in the p. part. D: C>T shows the base change; prefixes give the reference type. E: Genomic numbering uses g.; pathogenicity isn't part of the name.

questions.stem: A variant is found in 8% of the general population. How is it best described?

options.C: A variant of uncertain significance by definition

questions.explanation: A variant in ≥1% of the population is a polymorphism and is more likely benign. A: Common variants are rarely pathogenic for rare disease. B: Frequency doesn't define de novo status. C: VUS is a classification, not set by frequency. D: Somatic status is unrelated.

questions.stem: A woman with AD osteogenesis imperfecta carries a glycine substitution in one COL1A1 allele. The abnormal chains are incorporated into triple helices and disrupt them. What mechanism is this?
questions.explanation: The mutant protein interferes with the normal protein in the multimer. A: Haploinsufficiency is reduced quantity, not interference. B: No novel function is gained. D: Imprinting is parent-of-origin silencing. E: LOH applies to tumor suppressors.
questions.source: Genetic Variability and Disease, slide 37; reading p2

questions.stem: How many disease-causing variants does a typical individual exome contain?
questions.explanation: Of ~20,000 exome variants, only ~1–2 are disease-causing. A: Total variants. B: Non-synonymous. C: Rare variants. D: Homozygous rare variants.

questions.stem: A rare missense variant is found in a gene that fits the patient's phenotype, but the evidence is insufficient to call it either benign or pathogenic. How is it classified?
questions.explanation: A VUS is the middle ACMG category, used when evidence is insufficient either way. A: Likely benign requires evidence favoring benign. B: A polymorphism is defined by frequency ≥1%; this variant is rare. D: Likely pathogenic requires evidence favoring pathogenicity. E: Pathogenic requires strong evidence.
